node.title: Re^3: Finding the difference between two dates including milliseconds (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi Anonymous,

AFAIK [mod://DateTime] doesn't accept strings at all; I'm not sure where you're getting that specific format from? Again, please show the code you are trying, along with some sample input, the expected output for that sample input, and the actual output of the code including exact error messages, if any - see [id://174051]

[mod://DateTime::Format::Strptime] will accept the data in almost any format including the one in the OP, but you'll have to build an appropriate pattern according to its documentation. So something like "%Y-%m-%d ..." - scroll down in the documentation to see all the different tokens and pick the ones appropriate for your format.

Update: Hint: [href://?node_id=3989;BIT=DateTime%3A%3AFormat%3A%3AStrptime|Super search] is your friend, among the first search results you'll find example code posted by myself and others.

Update 2: Hm, I'm guessing you may have gotten the string "Mon Mar 27 05:54:08 CDT 2009" from [http://stackoverflow.com/questions/726289/how-do-i-convert-a-date-into-epoch-time-in-perl/726414|this] StackOverflow post. Note that that code uses [mod://Time::ParseDate], and not [mod://DateTime]. Follow the links I've given you and you'll find the appropriate documentation including example code.

Regards,
-- Hauke D
